subject: how long do probability function tests take?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: how long do probability function tests take?
parts:
The Wiener test is burning a hole in my computer with -j4 has been
running for nearly two hours. Is that just because it has so
many arguments? How long should it take to run? When do these
tests get run? There doesn't seem to be enough time to run them
per pull request.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: how long do probability function tests take?
parts:
On Saturday, August 27, 2016 at 2:50:18 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
The Wiener test is burning a hole in my computer with -j4 has been
running for nearly two hours.  Is that just because it has so
many arguments?  How long should it take to run?  When do these
tests get run?  There doesn't seem to be enough time to run them
per pull request.

Well, there are 1602 Wiener tests on develop. You can set N_TESTS to -4 in make/local to try to put them into batches of 400 but you might not have enough RAM to handle that. If you tell me what branch are you on, I can try them in the Stan Underground Bunker.

But in general, our testing framework makes it prohibitive to implement densities with many templated arguments. Something like this essentially has to be done on something like Yeti where we can set up a job array of 1602.

Ben

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: how long do probability function tests take?
parts:
In short, it takes a while. It's one of the reasons we offload it to Jenkins and haven't forced every developer to check locally.

I understand how Yeti works well enough to be able to create a job from outside to offload to Jenkins. That might be useful. Even for Jenkins to offload to it.


Daniel

parts:
I'm doing that. The problem now is that

stan/math/prim/scal/err/check_positive.hpp

seems to be broken. Or it's not being used right in wiener_log.

Specifically, this:

template <typename T_y, bool is_vec>
struct positive {
static bool check(const char* function,
const char* name,
const T_y& y) {
// have to use not is_unsigned. is_signed will be false
// floating point types that have no unsigned versions.
if (!boost::is_unsigned<T_y>::value && !(y > 0))
domain_error(function, name, y,
"is ", ", but must be > 0!");
return true;
}
};


winds up matching a std::vector in T_y and then failing because
you can't do (y > 0) with a vector. I don't see any array or
matrix specializations for this. Is something that needs to be included
not included?

Either the test framework isn't calling this or isn't calling it with
a std::vector or the test framework isn't getting called.

OK, I give up. Can you fix this one? I pushed my broken test
into a regular unit test. I don't trust running the test framework
not to destroy my machine after it got so hot running the tests for
two hours yesterday.

- Bob
